title: Finding and Recovering Work
description: Practice finding and recovering work through a concrete team scenario.

blocks.content: Even with Git, it can feel like you've lost work - maybe you reset to the wrong commit, or deleted a branch by mistake. Git has a safety net called the **reflog** that records every position HEAD has been at, even if the commits are no longer on any branch.

## The Reflog

View the reflog:
```
git reflog
```

Example output:
```
a3f9c12 HEAD@{0}: commit: add search feature
7b2d441 HEAD@{1}: reset: moving to HEAD~1
e1a8009 HEAD@{2}: commit: initial commit
```

Each line shows a position HEAD was at and what action moved it there. Even commits that were "lost" by a reset usually appear here.

Recover a lost commit by checking it out or resetting to it:
```
git checkout a3f9c12        # go to that commit directly
git reset --hard a3f9c12    # move current branch back to it
```

## Other Useful Recovery Commands

Search all commits for a specific string:
```
git log -S "function broken"
```

Find which commit introduced a bug using binary search:
```
git bisect start
git bisect bad          # current commit is broken
git bisect good e1a8009  # this old commit was fine
# Git now checks out commits for you to test. Mark each:
git bisect good
git bisect bad
# When done:
git bisect reset
```

See all changes to a specific file across history:
```
git log -p -- path/to/file
```

blocks.question: You ran `git reset --hard` and lost some commits. Where can you find them?
options: They are permanently gone - git reset is irreversible
In the reflog, which records every position HEAD has been at
blocks.explanation: The reflog is Git's safety net. It records every position HEAD has been at, even commits that no longer appear on any branch. After a `git reset --hard`, the lost commits still appear in the reflog for a while (usually 90 days). You can recover them by checking out the commit hash shown in the reflog.

blocks.prompt: Show the reflog to find recent HEAD positions.
